steps.text: Mix tomato soup, vegetable oil, sugar, vinegar, dry mustard, salt, celery seeds, black pepper, and garlic powder in a large jar with a lid. For thicker dressing, stir in cornstarch. Serve immediately or refrigerate overnight for best flavor.

raw_recipe.headline: Dorothy Lynch Style Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Mix up a batch of this tangy tomato dressing for your taco salads.
raw_recipe.name: Dorothy Lynch Style Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Mix tomato soup, vegetable oil, sugar, vinegar, dry mustard, salt, celery seeds, black pepper, and garlic powder in a large jar with a lid. For thicker dressing, stir in cornstarch. Serve immediately or refrigerate overnight for best flavor.

review.reviewBody: What a great dressing! I found it when I was looking at the Chicken Fiesta Salad reviews, and another reviewer mentioned this dressing. I am not a tomato soup fan AT ALL, so I was leary. I tasted it right after I made it, and still wasn't sure, but after letting it sit and blend the flavors, I was so happy!! I just finished making it for the second time, this time, I put everything in my Magic Bullet. Used only 1/2-3/4 cup oil, and about 1/2 the sugar. We actually use it on all salads for a different flavor. So good! Thanks!!

Oh my, this was great! Hubs and I both really liked it. I made half this recipe to try it out. I followed the recipe with the exception of cutting the sugar in half, using 3 T. for my half recipe. I also didn’t use the cornstarch. I whisked everything up in a bowl and transferred it to a jar with a tight-fitting lid and shook it to further emulsify it. We enjoyed this on Chicken Fiesta Salad, also on this site. And to use up the remaining half can of tomato soup, I made half a recipe of Tomato Soup Spice Cake, also here on AR.

I never rate a recipe unless made exactly as written, How can you? This was not the best at first because I used store brand tomato soup. The next time I used Campbell's and it made all the difference in the world. At first I used a jar and shook it up, it separated. The blender is the only way to make it mix together well and stay mixed. Although I use it frequently, it stays in the fridge for much longer than several months. The rating is for the way it was written--not specific enough.

Worked out as close to perfect as possible. Love DL's dressing. But I mixed all ingredients together except the soup. Heated briefly in micro. Allows the seeds , etc to infuse quicker, more pronounced. Let sit for a few. Then the soup. I used walnut oil for health benefits. Also, smoked paprika. Tones down the vinegar bite and actually improves the flavor. About a Tbsp to start. You'll love it. Tom T in Dallas

This recipe is absolutely amazing. My husband loves Dorothy lynch so I was skeptical but he didn't even notice it wasn't his usual salad dressing. I did use 1 tablespoon of cornstarch. It turned out the perfect texture. The second time I made it I used slightly less vinegar and slightly more sugar and I added 1 cup of shredded cheddar cheese. Then I pulsed it in the blender and this is now our favorite salad dressing.
This was very close to the store-bought dressing. I left the garlic out (hubby is allergic) and used Splenda instead of sugar. It is delicious! So happy to find this recipe!

I made this with fresh tomato sauce that I made from my homegrown tomatoes and it was fantastic! I didn't add the oil and backed way off of the sugar and used brown sugar instead of white and Braggs Apple cider vinegar. If the tomato soup isn't something you want to use (gotten bad reviews) and you don't have your own home grown sauce, maybe try stewed tomatoes instead. It definitely had the Dorothy flavor without a lot of calories.

This was excellent and easy. I first made it per the recipe but with only 1/2 cup sugar. That seemed to be a good choice as it came out sweet, but not "too"
Later, I made some adjustments. Pepper total 1/2 tsp, garlic powder total 1/4 tsp. corn starch total 1 tsp.
Then I read the actual mfgr bottle label and added 1/2 tsp onion powder and 1 tsp rice flour.
All of the changes made modest improvements.

I also add 1/4 tsp potassium sorbate solution to prevent mold and yeast spoiling. This is found on Amazon under winemaking supplies and some is in the factory dressing. I do this for all tomato sauces and salad dressings that aren't used right away. It really works.
I reduced sugar to 1/2 C. Increased the vinegar to 3/4 C A little more pepper an some fresh basil … blended it on low
I cut the sugar to 1/4 cup and found it still sweet. I may omit the sugar altogether next time, but to get it less sweet I added more vinegar.

I used my blender for making this dressing, I started with 1/2 cup of oil and then added in more until it reached the right flavor as another reviewer suggested, probably 3/4 cup total. No need for the optional cornstarch. My husband couldn't stop raving about this dressing, he really loved it, as did my son. It was tad too sweet for me, but then I don't put sugar on anything...so that is just me. I can't compare to the store version, since I've never had it. We used on a regular green salad.

I made this exactly as stated but just cut down the sugar a little bit. It is TOTALLY like the bottled Dorothy Lynch dressing I used to be able to buy from my local grocery store. Made me so happy and brought back memories. I made a Cobb salad to share with neighbors here for lunch. It was a hit because a few never had this dressing. TY TY
I was able to make a sugar free version with just Splenda, since they don't have one. Tastes just like the original. Thank you!
I used powdered onion, celery seed, and left out the onion and celery.
Very good and I can control the sodium in this recipe for our sodium limits. I use half of the salt and used pink Himalayan. This is Better then the bottle of dressing u can buy! Thank you!
My husband and I loved this dressing. I’m planning to make it again to use on taco salad. Thank you for posting the recipe.
I loved it. I used 1/2 olive oil and 1/2 avacado oil. I also used Splenda as the sweetener.
i have been making this dressing for a long time , my mom used to make it alot also and still buy it also .my kids use it for fries and other things
Just like my favorite dressing that I have ever had. A must try recipe
